title: Annihilators of affine limits of formal kernels and cokernels
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $I$ a quasi-coherent ideal, $F,G$ coherent formal $I$-modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and $\alpha:F\to G$. Let $k,c$ be a limiting kernel fork and colimiting cokernel cofork [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. For any affine open $V$, put $L(M)=\varprojlim_n\Gamma(V,M_{n+1})$, an $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$-module [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine]. Then $\operatorname{Ann}_A L(k)=\operatorname{Ann}_A\operatorname{Ker}(L(\alpha))$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_A L(c)=\operatorname{Ann}_A\operatorname{Coker}(L(\alpha))$.

source.place: Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), affine kernel description and exact restriction, together with Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine); verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087X and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087W

proof.text: Obtain Noetherianness of the open subscheme from the open embedding, and Noetherianness of its affine section ring from IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian. Apply AdicCompletion.isNoetherianRing to the section ideal. Prove the finite-module property is closed under subobjects by mono_iff_injective and isNoetherian_of_injective, and under quotients by epi_iff_surjective and Module.Finite.of_surjective. Thus its full-subcategory inclusion preserves kernels and cokernels.

Choose the affine finite completed-module equivalence and the natural comparison for the concrete section-limit functor from the affine-limit model. Only proof data is chosen; no object or definition is built from arbitrary existence.

Map the given limiting kernel fork and colimiting cokernel cofork successively through restriction, the equivalence, the finite-module inclusion and restriction of scalars. Restriction preserves finite limits and colimits; the equivalence preserves all existing ones; the inclusion preserves these two operations by the closure assertions just proved; scalar restriction preserves both. This gives preservation of the two parallel-pair diagrams by the composite functor.

Transport both preservation assertions to the concrete section-limit functor along the natural isomorphism. Compare its mapped fork and cofork with the categorical kernel and cokernel using uniqueness of (co)limits. Compose these isomorphisms with ModuleCat.kernelIsoKer and ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient. Apply LinearEquiv.annihilator_eq to their underlying linear equivalences to obtain the two desired equalities.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 087W and Lemma 087X; affine-model transport separated from the proved finite-module closure, (co)limit preservation and annihilator comparison. Sources checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087W and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087X.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModule_limit_annihilators
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (F G : CoherentFormalModule X I) (α : F ⟶ G)
    (k : KernelFork α) (c : CokernelCofork α) (hk : IsLimit k) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (V : X.affineOpens) :
    Module.annihilator Γ(X, V.1)
      (limit (k.pt.obj ⋙ SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)) :
        ModuleCat Γ(X, V.1)) =
      Module.annihilator Γ(X, V.1) (LinearMap.ker
        (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom
          (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)))).hom) ∧
    Module.annihilator Γ(X, V.1)
      (limit (c.pt.obj ⋙ SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)) :
        ModuleCat Γ(X, V.1)) =
      Module.annihilator Γ(X, V.1)
        (↥(limit (G.obj ⋙ SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)) :
          ModuleCat Γ(X, V.1)) ⧸ LinearMap.range
          (lim.map (Functor.whiskerRight α.hom
            (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op V.1)))).hom)
